question.text: A simple harmonic oscillator has an amplitude <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and time period <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mi>π</mi></math> second. Assuming the oscillation starts from its mean position, the time required by it to travel from<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo> </mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>A</mi></math> will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text:
From phasor diagram particle has to move from P to Q in a circle of radius equal to amplitude of SHM.

cosϕ=3 A2 A=32

⇒ϕ=π6

Now, π6=ωt

⇒π6=2πTt

⇒π6=2π6πt

⇒t=π2

So, x=2
